q: The concept of Wadge reducibility (continuous reducibility) defines the Wadge hierarchy. In the Baire space, it is well-founded and almost linear, meaning:
opts: Every two sets are Wadge equivalent
Every two sets are Wadge comparable (A ≤_W B or B ≤_W Ā) by the Wadge-Martin theorem
The hierarchy has only countably many levels
All analytic sets have the same Wadge degree
exp: Wadge's lemma (using determinacy): for any A, B ⊆ ℕᴺ, either A ≤_W B or B ≤_W Ā (complement of A). The hierarchy is well-founded and almost linear, giving a fine classification of topological complexity.
